Lessons.Title: Completing the Square (Part 3)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: adapt completing the square to nonmonic quadratic equations ax²+bx+c=0, first dividing by nonzero a and then completing a monic square; correct the misconception that (2x+3)² has middle coefficient6x. Independently authored Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 7 Lesson 14 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/14/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/14/index.html (CC BY 4.0).
Original equation 2x²+8x−10=0. Divide by2 to obtain x²+4x−5=0, or x²+4x=5. Add half-of-four squared,4, to both sides: (x+2)²=9, so x+2=±3 and x=1 or−5. Original check at1:2+8−10=0; at−5:50−40−10=0.

Second model 3x²−6x−9=0. Divide by3: x²−2x−3=0; move−3: x²−2x=3. Add1 both sides: (x−1)²=4; roots x=3 or−1. This demonstrates preserving signs across division and using a correct completing term after normalizing leading coefficient.

Student task: compare a student's incorrect attempt to complete square without dividing a, solve two nonmonic quadratics, and expand (2x+3)² to locate cross-term error. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 for initial coefficient normalization, valid complete-square terms, both checked roots and reasoned critique.

KeyConcepts.Title: Normalize leading coefficient
KeyConcepts.Definition: Divide both sides of ax²+bx+c=0 by nonzero a before monic completion.

KeyConcepts.Title: Complete after normalization

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Completing square before normalizing a without adjusting coefficients
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The missing-square term depends on b/a.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Dropping 2 from scaled square's mixed term
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Two cross products must be included.

SummaryPoints: Normalize nonmonic quadratic then complete monic square.
Scaled squares still require two cross terms.
